title: Room-by-room design and contractor record

workflow.remainingOrder: Proposed continuation; confirm as the user proceeds.
workflow.rule: Review all four floors and refine room-specific concepts from labeled images. Preserve each revision and append dated feedback. Remaining unphotographed second-floor spaces need separate development.
workflow.approvalRule: A liked render is visual direction only. Products, quantities, dimensions, fabrication and site conditions need explicit records; do not treat render pixels as construction dimensions.
workflow.revisionRule: Never silently overwrite prior selections. Append dated feedback, record affected item IDs, supersede old proposals and update the active revision.
workflow.reviewScope: Original Option 1: 24 spaces, 45 daytime views and 24 matching night views; Bedroom 5 is proposed new construction.

confirmed: Warm, welcoming, calm and sophisticated modern home with a five-star-hotel/showcase feel.
Budget-conscious phased work; replace existing items when it materially improves the result.
Visible wall detailing and layered lighting with straightforward construction.
Warm wood, warm neutral backgrounds and black/dark accents.
Green through plants/leafy stems, with neutral artwork and textiles; preferred previews A/C/E in green-black exploration.
Use the real white-brick house exterior and real model-home photos, with the blueprint for room relationships.
Stair interpretation must respect the user's quarter-turn/curved rise to an intermediate landing then onward straight flight; do not invent a continuous freestanding spiral.

FB-015: give each bedroom an individual identity within the shared warm modern palette. Reserve the continuous illuminated walnut headboard band for the owners suite; use simpler distinct treatments in the three guest bedrooms.
FB-016: all four bedrooms use hard wood flooring with separate loose rugs; the penthouse is included. Preserve individual room identities. Entry flooring should match second-floor oak.
Original Option 1 palette only: warm mineral, walnut, natural oak, ivory, dark accents and plants.
Most finishes replaced; all new furniture budgeted. No Option 2 owned-furniture assumptions.
Media wall remains smooth and restrained, with TV as focal point; gym stays empty.
Bedroom 5 has not been built and must be included as new room construction.
pending: Exact wall colors and manufacturer samples.
Roman Clay versus limewash final selection by room.
Product SKUs, installer quotations and purchasing authorization.
Measured as-built dimensions and full hidden elevations.

feedbackLog.userFeedback: i like the just plants better
feedbackLog.interpretation: Prefer A/C/E from green-black exploration: plants supply green; black accents, warm neutral art/textiles and wood retained.

feedbackLog.userFeedback: Generate each room one at a time starting with first floor entry, then office, media room, gym; give feedback on each until done; derive different angles from blueprint and original angle; remember all feedback and build details for the general contractor.
feedbackLog.interpretation: Begin entry revision r01 with original and derived views. Maintain revisioned room records, finish schedules, decision logs, evidence and open measurement/product questions.

feedbackLog.userFeedback: Explore inspirational quotes painted or in 3D letters above the entry door AND on the wall below the railing above the entry archway. Suggested doorway wording: “Take the road less traveled by” — Robert Frost. Asked for design thoughts.
feedbackLog.interpretation: A new idea to explore, not approval of lettering, exact wording, typography, material or both placements. Preserve the r01 render as the baseline.

feedbackLog.userFeedback: For above the archway, maybe use “Home is where the Heart is”; designer to decide on the leaving-house quote.
feedbackLog.interpretation: Explore the suggested welcome phrase above the arch and a designer-chosen departing motto over the front door. For r02 use “Take the road less traveled” without author attribution, with raised charcoal letters over the door and smaller painted lettering over the arch. Both treatments remain visual proposals for feedback.

feedbackLog.userFeedback: Archway quote should be a little smaller and painted on. Front entrance quote should be smaller and installed 3D letters. Wants a fancier chandelier hanging through two floors like a shower or bulbs at different lengths, visible from the second floor.
feedbackLog.interpretation: Reduce both inscriptions from r02; establish painted arch lettering and dimensional front-door lettering as preferred treatments. Replace small three-globe branch pendant with a tall staggered pendant cascade in the existing double-height void. Designer proposes matte-black hardware with warm opal globes; exact fixture/material details remain open.

feedbackLog.userFeedback: What if the doors on the left and right were a darker color? Asked whether this would be too much.
feedbackLog.interpretation: Explore darker finishes for both existing glass side-door pairs. Designer recommends a deep warm charcoal with a slight brown undertone in a satin trim-enamel appearance on the door leaves/glazing beads, while retaining light surrounding casings. Color/material choice is under discussion, not an approved change to r03.

feedbackLog.userFeedback: ok let’s render that
feedbackLog.interpretation: Authorized preview of the recommended deep warm-charcoal side-door leaves with satin appearance and light surrounding casings. Render both existing entry angles. This is approval to explore visually, not approval of a specific paint product or final finish.

feedbackLog.userFeedback: B
feedbackLog.interpretation: Selected option B from r04 review: try a slightly lighter charcoal on both glazed side-door pairs. This requests a new comparison preview, not final color or paint-product approval.

feedbackLog.userFeedback: does this conflict with the rest of the rooms we decided on for the design scheme?
feedbackLog.interpretation: Requests a cohesion assessment of the r05 entry against the preferred great-room, owner-bedroom and dining references. No final shade, finish or room approval is implied. Designer assessment: warm-charcoal glazed doors, light trim, walnut accents, mineral wall texture, plant green and opal/dark-metal lighting fit the selected direction. Current entry render has more amber, knotty flooring and warmer/more mottled walls than the selected room references; recommend calmer natural-oak appearance and subtle warm stone/mushroom undertones in the next refinement. Keep the dramatic fixture concentrated in the tall entry and the personal inscriptions local to the entry. These are recommendations, not newly approved specifications.

feedbackLog.userFeedback: Make the entry changes and render the rest of floor one together, with multiple angles per room based on blueprint and original photos, so the whole floor can be reviewed at once.
feedbackLog.interpretation: Authorizes calmer natural-oak appearance and subtler stone/mushroom entry walls, retaining option B warm-charcoal doors, inscriptions and cascading chandelier. Expands review scope to entry, office, media, gym and Bath #3 as one coordinated set. This explicitly supersedes the earlier one-room-at-a-time restriction for this floor. Alternate views remain inferred and Bath #3 has no original photo. Visual preferences and finish directions are not product/fabrication approval.
feedbackLog.resultingRevision: entry r06; office/media/gym/bath r01; coordinated floor review r01

feedbackLog.scope: floors 1–3 refinements, missing living room and all-bedroom flooring
feedbackLog.userFeedback: Entry: match second-floor wood color. Office: TV and soundbar in north cabinetry, artwork and small printer cabinet right of entry door. Media: clear entry doors, collectible shelves right of doors, less intense TV wall, soundbar, ceiling and behind-sofa speakers. Great room: sibling artworks above both consoles. Kitchen: better island lights. Dining: explore larger table for ten versus square twelve, fill space below high window. Living room: baby grand, Cloud couch, sheer drapes, two blueprint-derived angles. Sunroom: rectangular six-seat table, better chandelier, sheer drapes. All bedrooms: hard floors with loose rug under beds. Owner bedroom: 55-inch TV and soundbar instead of dresser art, art above bed, platform and bedside underside LEDs. Owner bath: artwork above tub. Bedroom 2: correct bed/desk/door layout; clarified headboard WEST and entry at southern WEST wall, desk right of EAST window. Laundry: graphic and exact wording “Rinse and repeat..”. Clarified oak/rug applies to penthouse bedroom too.
feedbackLog.interpretation: Preserve the individual bedroom identities and common warm modern palette. Propose rectangular 108 × 42 in dining table for ten, subject to actual circulation survey. Use plan-informed living room and explicitly record Bedroom 2 closet/door conflict rather than claiming its new layout is surveyed. All new images are proposals; measurements, products and trade details remain unselected.

scheduleSnapshot.material: Smooth subtle stone/mushroom mineral or plaster-like appearance; low visual movement, without peach cast or coarse trowel ridges. Exact finish system remains to select.
scheduleSnapshot.location: Entrance-facing arch wall, from baseboard around arch to underside of upper overlook; rendered arch returns match but sample/finish boundary needs approval.
scheduleSnapshot.preparation: Remove wallpaper and adhesive; inspect for damage/stains; repair and skim smooth as required; use manufacturer's compatible primer and coating schedule.
scheduleSnapshot.installation: Thin overlapping hand-troweled coats by experienced applicator; target restrained tonal movement. Price low-contact unsealed and contact-area compatible topcoat options with samples.
scheduleSnapshot.dimensions: Field-measure wall planes, arch radius/reveals and height; deduct opening; no measured quantity yet.
scheduleSnapshot.procurement: Exact product/color, coverage allowance, batch, sealer and applicator sample not approved.

scheduleSnapshot.material: Premium washable matte acrylic in warm ivory; exact manufacturer/color TBD.
scheduleSnapshot.location: Remaining gallery walls and coordinating center-hall wall areas.
scheduleSnapshot.preparation: Remove wallpaper residue, repair and prime as substrate requires; review wall texture under actual daylight.
scheduleSnapshot.installation: Full coating system to selected manufacturer's instructions; sample adjoining mineral finish to coordinate undertones.
scheduleSnapshot.dimensions: Area to be measured; exclude doors, glazing and trim.
scheduleSnapshot.procurement: Choose product, color and sheen after room review.

scheduleSnapshot.item: Light outer casings, jambs and baseboards
scheduleSnapshot.material: Smooth warm-white durable trim enamel, proposed satin/low-sheen appearance.
scheduleSnapshot.location: Retain existing outer decorative casings/head trim, fixed jambs and baseboards in warm white. Movable glazed side-door leaves are separately described in E-T02. Preserve existing profiles and clear glazing.
scheduleSnapshot.preparation: Identify existing coating, adhesion-test and prepare with compatible primer.
scheduleSnapshot.installation: Protect glazing and hinges; test clearance after recoating; no blanket trim replacement assumed.
scheduleSnapshot.dimensions: Measure linear lengths and door leaves on site.
scheduleSnapshot.procurement: Final sheen and hardware finish sample pending.

scheduleSnapshot.material: Natural light-medium oak appearance with quieter straight grain, minimal knotting and matte finish; avoid orange/amber coloration.
scheduleSnapshot.location: Entry/gallery continuing through center hall; transitions coordinated with office, gym and media room.
scheduleSnapshot.preparation: Inspect existing floor material, wear layer, condition, subfloor and moisture before selecting method.
scheduleSnapshot.installation: Price option A: retain/refinish existing floor if feasible. Option B: replace with prefinished engineered oak; proposed 6–7.5 inch plank width and at least 3 mm wear layer are design targets only. Verify selected product's substrate/installation requirements. The render shows a changed plank direction/width. Refinishing would retain existing plank dimensions, direction and species; it cannot reproduce a different floor assembly. Color outcome requires a test patch.
scheduleSnapshot.dimensions: No measured area; verify thresholds, door clearances and first stair rise before any floor-height change.
scheduleSnapshot.procurement: Species, grade, plank width, finish sample, SKU, delivery and waste allowance remain TBD.

scheduleSnapshot.material: Retain white balusters, newels and risers; dark smoked-brown wood handrail/treads.
scheduleSnapshot.location: Visible first-floor stair and upper gallery overlook.
scheduleSnapshot.preparation: Inspect existing wood/coating and condition; coordinate refinishing method across stair levels.
scheduleSnapshot.installation: Cosmetic treatment only in this proposal. Preserve turn, intermediate landing, upper flight, handrails and guard structure. Obtain verified stair survey before any modification.
scheduleSnapshot.dimensions: Risers, treads, landing, guard height and spacing are not specified from AI imagery; contractor to measure and verify applicable requirements.
scheduleSnapshot.procurement: No new baluster system or reconstructed stair included.

scheduleSnapshot.material: Designer proposal: slim matte-black canopy and individual fine black suspensions with warm opal-glass globes. A compatible retail multi-drop fixture/system is preferred for cost control; no product selected.
scheduleSnapshot.location: Within existing entrance-gallery void, suspended from the high ceiling. Light elements distributed through the upper-level viewing zone and lower gallery airspace, visible from the second-floor overlook.
scheduleSnapshot.designTargets: Airy staggered drops with a tall narrow composition. Roughly 8–10 small opal globes are the refined concept range only. The two renders vary in individual globe layout; specify one exact manufacturer drawing before ordering. Warm dimmable light; proposed 2700 K, CRI 90+. Preserve readable inscriptions and avoid glare at upper-floor eye level.
scheduleSnapshot.installation: Electrician/installer to verify ceiling attachment and structural support for actual fixture weight, box and canopy compatibility, power route, driver and dimmer compatibility, cable adjustment/strain relief and access for installation. Coordinate individual drop positions with upper guard, circulation, stair, windows and door operation. Plan safe cleaning, lamp/driver replacement and replacement-glass access before purchasing.
scheduleSnapshot.dimensions: Field-measure upper ceiling height, gallery void footprint, floor-to-floor levels, guard/rail positions, fixture envelope and each drop. Set lowest globe elevation and required clearances from site conditions and applicable requirements. Rendered suspension lengths are not installation dimensions.
scheduleSnapshot.procurement: Select manufacturer/model, canopy layout, overall weight, globe count/diameters, allowed suspension lengths, lamp or integrated-LED system, dimmer, service instructions, replacement parts and finish samples. Quote supply, access, support/power work, controls and installation separately. Do not order or fabricate from AI imagery.

feedback.scope: entry
feedback.userFeedback: Explore inspirational quotes painted or in 3D letters above the entry door AND on the wall below the railing above the entry archway. Suggested doorway wording: “Take the road less traveled by” — Robert Frost. Asked for design thoughts.
feedback.interpretation: A new idea to explore, not approval of lettering, exact wording, typography, material or both placements. Preserve the r01 render as the baseline.

feedback.scope: entry
feedback.userFeedback: For above the archway, maybe use “Home is where the Heart is”; designer to decide on the leaving-house quote.
feedback.interpretation: Explore the suggested welcome phrase above the arch and a designer-chosen departing motto over the front door. For r02 use “Take the road less traveled” without author attribution, with raised charcoal letters over the door and smaller painted lettering over the arch. Both treatments remain visual proposals for feedback.

feedback.scope: entry
feedback.userFeedback: Archway quote should be a little smaller and painted on. Front entrance quote should be smaller and installed 3D letters. Wants a fancier chandelier hanging through two floors like a shower or bulbs at different lengths, visible from the second floor.
feedback.interpretation: Reduce both inscriptions from r02; establish painted arch lettering and dimensional front-door lettering as preferred treatments. Replace small three-globe branch pendant with a tall staggered pendant cascade in the existing double-height void. Designer proposes matte-black hardware with warm opal globes; exact fixture/material details remain open.

feedback.scope: entry
feedback.userFeedback: What if the doors on the left and right were a darker color? Asked whether this would be too much.
feedback.interpretation: Explore darker finishes for both existing glass side-door pairs. Designer recommends a deep warm charcoal with a slight brown undertone in a satin trim-enamel appearance on the door leaves/glazing beads, while retaining light surrounding casings. Color/material choice is under discussion, not an approved change to r03.

feedback.scope: entry
feedback.userFeedback: ok let’s render that
feedback.interpretation: Authorized preview of the recommended deep warm-charcoal side-door leaves with satin appearance and light surrounding casings. Render both existing entry angles. This is approval to explore visually, not approval of a specific paint product or final finish.

feedback.scope: entry
feedback.userFeedback: B
feedback.interpretation: Selected option B from r04 review: try a slightly lighter charcoal on both glazed side-door pairs. This requests a new comparison preview, not final color or paint-product approval.

feedback.scope: entry / whole-house coordination
feedback.userFeedback: does this conflict with the rest of the rooms we decided on for the design scheme?
feedback.interpretation: Requests a cohesion assessment of the r05 entry against the preferred great-room, owner-bedroom and dining references. No final shade, finish or room approval is implied. Designer assessment: warm-charcoal glazed doors, light trim, walnut accents, mineral wall texture, plant green and opal/dark-metal lighting fit the selected direction. Current entry render has more amber, knotty flooring and warmer/more mottled walls than the selected room references; recommend calmer natural-oak appearance and subtle warm stone/mushroom undertones in the next refinement. Keep the dramatic fixture concentrated in the tall entry and the personal inscriptions local to the entry. These are recommendations, not newly approved specifications.

feedback.scope: first-floor coordinated review
feedback.userFeedback: Make the entry changes and render the rest of floor one together, with multiple angles per room based on blueprint and original photos, so the whole floor can be reviewed at once.
feedback.interpretation: Authorizes calmer natural-oak appearance and subtler stone/mushroom entry walls, retaining option B warm-charcoal doors, inscriptions and cascading chandelier. Expands review scope to entry, office, media, gym and Bath #3 as one coordinated set. This explicitly supersedes the earlier one-room-at-a-time restriction for this floor. Alternate views remain inferred and Bath #3 has no original photo. Visual preferences and finish directions are not product/fabrication approval.
feedback.resultingRevision: entry r06; office/media/gym/bath r01; coordinated floor review r01

feedback.scope: first floor revisions and start of second floor
feedback.userFeedback: Return entrance gallery to light doors; dark doors take too much attention. Office: entire north wall built out; large desk facing northwest instead of semicircle. Media: follow supplied vertical wood-slat TV-wall reference in our style; M2 door must be on west wall per blueprint. Gym: empty finished room with walls, mirror, selected quote and floor; owner will add equipment later. Start floor two.
feedback.interpretation: Warm ivory glazed side-door leaves replace charcoal on both room and gallery faces. feedback.userFeedback: Return entrance gallery to light doors; dark doors take too much attention. Office: entire north wall built out; large desk facing northwest instead of semicircle. Media: follow supplied vertical wood-slat TV-wall reference in our style; M2 door must be on west wall per blueprint. Gym: empty finished room with walls, mirror, selected quote and floor; owner will add equipment later. Start floor two.
feedback.interpretation: Warm ivory glazed side-door leaves replace charcoal on both room and gallery faces. Rectangular walnut office desk with southeast task chair facing northwest and full north-wall cabinetry replaces the curved desk and compact bookcase; south console remains omitted. Media south TV wall becomes walnut slats with long charcoal-front walnut console, subtle TV backlight and under-console light; west entry opening remains on perpendicular wall. Gym equipment, storage furniture and decor are deferred; retain northwest closet and separate bath access. Begin five photographed second-floor spaces with consistent finishes.

feedback.scope: floors 1–3 refinements, missing living room and all-bedroom flooring
feedback.userFeedback: Entry: match second-floor wood color. Office: TV and soundbar in north cabinetry, artwork and small printer cabinet right of entry door. Media: clear entry doors, collectible shelves right of doors, less intense TV wall, soundbar, ceiling and behind-sofa speakers. Great room: sibling artworks above both consoles. Kitchen: better island lights. Dining: explore larger table for ten versus square twelve, fill space below high window. Living room: baby grand, Cloud couch, sheer drapes, two blueprint-derived angles. Sunroom: rectangular six-seat table, better chandelier, sheer drapes. All bedrooms: hard floors with loose rug under beds. Owner bedroom: 55-inch TV and soundbar instead of dresser art, art above bed, platform and bedside underside LEDs. Owner bath: artwork above tub. Bedroom 2: correct bed/desk/door layout; clarified headboard WEST and entry at southern WEST wall, desk right of EAST window. Laundry: graphic and exact wording “Rinse and repeat..”. Clarified oak/rug applies to penthouse bedroom too.
feedback.interpretation: Preserve the individual bedroom identities and common warm modern palette. Propose rectangular 108 × 42 in dining table for ten, subject to actual circulation survey. Use plan-informed living room and explicitly record Bedroom 2 closet/door conflict rather than claiming its new layout is surveyed. All new images are proposals; measurements, products and trade details remain unselected.

feedback.scope: floors 1–3 refinements, missing living room and all-bedroom flooring
feedback.userFeedback: Entry: match second-floor wood color. Office: TV and soundbar in north cabinetry, artwork and small printer cabinet right of entry door. Media: clear entry doors, collectible shelves right of doors, less intense TV wall, soundbar, ceiling and behind-sofa speakers. Great room: sibling artworks above both consoles. Kitchen: better island lights. Dining: explore larger table for ten versus square twelve, fill space below high window. Living room: baby grand, Cloud couch, sheer drapes, two blueprint-derived angles. Sunroom: rectangular six-seat table, better chandelier, sheer drapes. All bedrooms: hard floors with loose rug under beds. Owner bedroom: 55-inch TV and soundbar instead of dresser art, art above bed, platform and bedside underside LEDs. Owner bath: artwork above tub. Bedroom 2: correct bed/desk/door layout; clarified headboard WEST and entry at southern WEST wall, desk right of EAST window. Laundry: graphic and exact wording “Rinse and repeat..”. Clarified oak/rug applies to penthouse bedroom too.
feedback.interpretation: Preserve the individual bedroom identities and common warm modern palette. Propose rectangular 108 × 42 in dining table for ten, subject to actual circulation survey. Use plan-informed living room and explicitly record Bedroom 2 closet/door conflict rather than claiming its new layout is surveyed. All new images are proposals; measurements, products and trade details remain unselected.
